newsitem.title: USA: Grand Union says some suppliers have pulled plug.
newsitem.headline: Grand Union says some suppliers have pulled plug.

text.p: A spokesman for Grand Union said "less than a handful" of suppliers had pulled the plug on deliveries to the supermarket giant amid concerns about its ability to meet its debt obligations.

"There's less than a handful of other suppliers who have been frightened by the media reports -- that are not necessarily true -- that have ceased some terms but we are working with them to get those terms back in order," said Donald Vaillancourt, vice president of communications at Grand Union.
Rumors circulated in the corporate debt market on Thursday that Pillsbury Foods, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, had stopped supplying the supermarket chain.
"I'm not going to confirm something specifically like that," Vaillancourt told Reuters from Grand Union's headquarters in Wayne, N.J.
He said C&S Wholesale Groceries of Brattleboro, Vt., was its chief supplier, providing about 75 percent of the items stocking Grand Union's shelves.
C&S Wholesale Groceries did not immediately return calls.
Officials at Pillsbury in Minneapolis declined to comment.

Grand Union bonds have seen a steep decline over the last two months on concerns over the firm's cash flows and its ability to meet its next coupon payment, due September 1. Despite the concerns Grand Union's 12 percent paper was quoted several points higher at 52-1/2 bid, 53-1/2 offer.
